summary.rationale: Gemma4 correctly normalises OCR garbles through semantic understanding (university name, year, exam name). RapidOCR finds the candidate name location but cannot fix character-level OCR errors. For structured multi-column Indian marksheet tables the regex + spatial heuristic approach fails due to token merging and column misalignment. Gemma4 vision-LLM is more robust for complex historical document layouts.
rapidocr_advantages: Found candidate name via position heuristic even if garbled
156 raw text regions - rich raw text for downstream fuzzy matching
Mean confidence score per token (0.72) useful for quality gating
No GPU required, ~8-9s inference on CPU
Correct grand total 925/1500 via bare-fraction fallback regex
No hallucination risk - outputs only what is literally on the page
gemma4_advantages: Semantic normalisation of OCR garbles: year, university, exam name
Cleaner subject list: 8 semantically coherent entries vs 16 over-parsed rows
Identifies document structure without column-alignment heuristics
Returns null for missing fields rather than wrong values
Handles merged tokens in dense headers that defeat classical pipelines
summary.onednn_note: PaddleOCR 3.4.0 with PaddlePaddle 3.3.1 could not be used directly due to an unfixable upstream C++ bug: NotImplementedError in onednn_instruction.cc:116 when loading PIR-format models. oneDNN is compiled INTO the PaddlePaddle binary and cannot be uninstalled without rebuilding from source. RapidOCR uses the same PP-OCRv4 models via ONNX Runtime and bypasses PaddlePaddle entirely.
